### Step 1: Calculate Moles of HNO3

Given:
- Mass of HNO3 solution = 300 g
- Mass percentage of HNO3 = 63%

The mass of pure HNO3 is:
\[ \text{Mass of pure HNO3} = 300 \, \text{g} \times 0.63 = 189 \, \text{g} \]

The molar mass of HNO3 is approximately 63 g/mol, so the moles of HNO3 is:
\[ \text{Moles of HNO3} = \frac{189 \, \text{g}}{63 \, \text{g/mol}} = 3 \, \text{mol} \]

### Step 2: Determine the Amount of Trinitroglycerin Produced

For the nitration of glycerin to trinitroglycerin, 3 moles of HNO3 produce 1 mole of trinitroglycerin (C3H5N3O9).

Therefore, 3 moles of HNO3 produce 1 mole of trinitroglycerin.

From 1 mole of trinitroglycerin, we get:

- 2.5 moles of CO2

Half of the trinitroglycerin (0.5 moles) would produce:
\[ 0.5 \times 4 = 2 \, \text{moles of gas} \]

Using the ideal gas law at standard conditions (1 mole of gas occupies 22.4 L):
\[ \text{Volume of gas} = 2 \times 22.4 \, \text{L} = 44.8 \, \text{L} \]
